summary.headline: Tata Capital Q4 FY26 PAT ex-exceptionals rose 51% YoY to INR1,459 crore (ex-motor finance); consolidated credit cost fell to 0.9%.
summary.overview: Ex-motor finance AUM reached INR2.52 lakh crore (+28% YoY, +8% QoQ) and consolidated AUM INR2.77 lakh crore (+20% YoY), within the 18-20% guided range. Credit costs fell to 0.8% ex-motor finance and 0.9% consolidated, with net NPA at 0.5% ex-MF. Motor Finance turned profitable at INR43 crore PAT in Q4 after breaking even in Q3, though its AUM fell 4% QoQ to INR25,390 crore. Management reiterated the FY28 guidance (23-25% AUM CAGR over FY25-FY28, ROA ~2%, cost-to-income 33-34%) and said FY27 cost of funds should be lower than FY26.

segments.name: Retail & SME
segments.commentary: Retail and SME make up 86% of AUM. Secured retail grew about 28% and SME growth picked up in Q3 and Q4 after the GST cut; unsecured retail is 10.3% of AUM with disbursements up about 50% YoY in Q4.

segments.name: Housing Finance (Tata Capital Housing Finance)
segments.commentary: AUM INR86,653 crore (+29% YoY), PAT +34% YoY in Q4 and +23% for FY26; ROA 2.6% in Q4, credit cost 0.1%, net NPA 0.3%, cost-to-income below 30% in Q4.

segments.name: Motor Finance
segments.commentary: Q4 PAT INR43 crore on AUM INR25,390 crore (-4% QoQ); non-Tata OEM share of new CV disbursements 26%; Q4 disbursements +32% QoQ; management expects growth to resume from H1 FY27.

segments.name: Corporate lending
segments.commentary: Modest increase in Q4 via clean energy, developer funding and opportunistic high-rated corporate lending; management cites yields around 11% (corporate) and 12-13% (developer), with ROA of 2.5% or more.

guidance_outlook: FY28 guidance: AUM growth 23-25% CAGR over FY25-FY28; management says high-yield growth will be above 25% to average 23-25%.
FY28 targets: ROA about 2% (consolidated), cost-to-income 33-34%; ROA guidance of 2.5-2.7% was cited in Q&A.
Credit cost target of about 1% by FY28, with 20-25bp of further reduction possible; opex reduction of about 15bp.
FY27 cost of funds expected lower than FY26 because of repricing of liabilities; incremental borrowing costs rose in March.
FY27 Motor Finance disbursements expected up about 80%+, but total CV book growth may be about 10% due to repayments; margins expected to improve slightly in FY27.
Branch network expected to grow 10-15% in FY27.
capex_capacity: 1,477 branches across 27 states and UTs; about 350 housing finance branches; plans to add branches in affordable and micro housing.
Customer base of 8.4 million; on-roll employees 29,816 as of March end.
Document Intelligence Engine has processed over 2 crore documents with 80+ bots, improving operations productivity by 35%.
Underwriting Assist adoption at 85%, cutting SME credit memo time from two days to 20 minutes.
demand_pricing: Quarter 4 disbursements crossed INR50,000 crore for the first time.
Fee income about 1.1% of AUM, unchanged QoQ, per management.
Management says April bounce rates fell versus Q4 and collections in Surat and Morbi were as strong as March.
Tightening in certain MSME sub-segments (hotels, travel) and CV/construction equipment is being monitored closely after West Asia conflict.
Motor Finance: non-Tata OEM share of new CV disbursements reached 26%; repricing of legacy borrowings about 95% done in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the West Asia conflict on clients and segments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no significant or even marginal impact so far; SME and large corporate clients hold raw material stocks and are passing on cost increases, with MSME kept under closer watch.

qa_highlights.question: Why did credit cost fall from 1.4% in FY25 to 1.2% in FY26, and how much is due to AI?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to analytics-led underwriting, GenAI-based model building and conservative credit policy together; quarterly consolidated credit cost fell from 1.6% in Q1 to 0.9% in Q4 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Will the CV book keep growing given the cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Disbursements are planned to grow about 80%+ in FY27, but book growth may be only about 10% because of repayments on the matured book; growth should pick up in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Expected NIM and spread trajectory in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects margins to improve slightly as high-yield unsecured, Motor Finance and affordable housing grow faster; Q4 NIM is better than the full-year average on a daily-average basis.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY28 ROA target achievable and what are the levers?
qa_highlights.answer: Levers are cost-to-income reduction via technology and AI, branch productivity from adding products per branch, and scale benefits; management said credit cost of about 1% and opex savings of about 15bp, with NIM plus fee making up the rest.

qa_highlights.question: Is the stress in April visible in PL/BL and in the SME book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said SME/CV/unsecured stress has not appeared in April, with bounce rates lower than Q4 and no material stress in Surat/Morbi; some MSME sub-segments were tightened as a precaution.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict: second- and third-order effects on MSME, CV and construction equipment; El Nino and food inflation risk to rural demand.
Rising incremental borrowing costs after March; management expects FY27 cost of funds to be lower than FY26 but this depends on fresh borrowing rates.
Motor Finance growth resumption in H1 FY27 and whether credit costs keep falling; Q1 and Q2 are seen as the watch periods.
Mark-to-market losses on private equity and listed investments in March, which hit non-interest income; management calls them temporary.
Unsecured book growth (currently 10.3% of AUM, target 15%) and whether credit costs stay in check as disbursements rise.
summary.management_tone: Confident and detailed on delivery of FY26 guidance and asset quality improvement, but cautious on MSME and CV exposure due to the West Asia conflict. Management was evasive on specific cost-of-funds and yield targets for FY27, pointing to direction rather than numbers.
key_quotes: In the first year itself, we broke even in quarter 3 and have made money in quarter 4 and which will keep increasing going forward with every passing half year or so.
So what dealers are seeing is that the phase of the volumes going down , the monthly volumes going down is over.
We are increasing exposure to used commercial vehicles and small and mid-commercial vehicles while reducing our heavy commercial vehicle concentration.

adds.what: Branch network expansion, 10-15% growth in FY27 (Tata Capital branches, currently 1,477 across 27 states and UTs)

growth.why: FY28 guidance of 23-25% AUM CAGR (FY25-FY28) reiterated, with Q4 ex-MF AUM +28% YoY and disbursements above INR50,000 crore (+32% YoY), and branches to grow 10-15% in FY27; backing is partly specific (branch count, disbursement run-rate, Motor Finance growth from H1 FY27) but no concrete capacity or order numbers for the AUM CAGR.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects margins to improve slightly in FY27 as high-yield unsecured, Motor Finance and affordable housing grow faster; Q4 NIM is above the full-year average and net total income margin held at 6.5% in Q4, with cost-of-funds guided lower in FY27 and opex reduction of about 15bp targeted for FY28.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Branch network guided to grow 10-15% in FY27 from 1,477 branches across 27 states and UTs, with plans to add affordable and micro housing branches (about 350 housing branches today).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q4 disbursements crossed INR50,000 crore (+32% YoY), ex-MF AUM grew 28% YoY, and FY27 Motor Finance disbursements are guided up about 80%+, though CV book growth may be only about 10% from repayments.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY26 PAT ex-non-recurring grew 36%, above the 32-35% guidance, and credit cost fell from 1.6% in Q1 to 0.9% in Q4 FY26, but management reiterated rather than raised FY28 targets (23-25% AUM CAGR, ROA ~2%).

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: West Asia conflict is flagged for MSME, CV and construction equipment with tightening in hotels and travel sub-segments, incremental borrowing costs rose in March, and Motor Finance growth resumption from H1 FY27 is still unproven with the book down 4% QoQ.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management is pushing products per branch and unsecured retail, which is 10.3% of AUM against a 15% target, but no specific new product launch was named.

rows.label: Cost of funds lower in FY27
rows.why: Liability repricing is about 95% done in FY26 and cost of funds is 7.1% (-5bp QoQ), though incremental borrowing costs rose in March and management gave direction, not numbers.

rows.label: Motor Finance growth resumes from H1 FY27
rows.why: Motor Finance turned profitable at INR43 crore PAT in Q4 after breakeven in Q3, non-Tata OEM share of new CV disbursements reached 26%, but AUM fell 4% QoQ to INR25,390 crore.

rows.label: Cost-to-income to 33-34% by FY28
rows.why: FY26 cost-to-income was 38.3% (-335bp YoY), the Document Intelligence Engine has lifted operating productivity 35%, and opex savings of about 15bp are targeted.
